steps.note: A CONNECT sent over TLS. The 8.0.0 oracle serves only HTTP/1.1 inside the outer TLS (RelayConnectHandler: an SslHandler is already in the pipeline, so configurePipelines without detection); upstream fix 40939d794 defers detection on every CONNECT, so the snapshot classifies the decrypted first bytes as it does in a cleartext tunnel: a nested TLS record is terminated, the h2c preface is served as HTTP/2. The tunnelled bytes follow the CONNECT after a second (chunkMillis): the oracle opens its loopback to itself before it answers 200, and bytes that arrive while it does so are lost, so a 200 ms gap raced against a cold oracle.

tcp.text:
GET /hello HTTP/1.1
Host: mocked.example.test:443
Connection: close

steps.note: plaintext HTTP/1.1 inside a CONNECT over TLS: matched

tcp.text:
GET /unmatched HTTP/1.1
Host: mocked.example.test:443
Connection: close

steps.note: plaintext HTTP/1.1 inside a CONNECT over TLS: unmatched, so proxied to the unresolvable target: 502
h2c prior knowledge inside a CONNECT over TLS: the preface, an empty SETTINGS and a HEADERS frame (GET /hello, END_STREAM) on stream 1
a malformed TLS ClientHello inside a CONNECT over TLS: 8.0.0 parses it as HTTP (/bad-request, proxied: 502); after the fix it is a TLS record, refused with a decode_error alert
a TLS 1.2 ClientHello inside a CONNECT over TLS: after the fix the nested handshake is answered with the server's flight
the HTTP/1.1 and (after the fix) the h2c request reached the data plane
